meta.note: Items marked fromC were read from C headers or build output, not from the docs.

events.name: game.new
caveats: game.new and menu.open have no fields at all: the event is the moment itself.
events.when: The player starts a new game, before the first map loads.

events.name: save.begin
events.when: A save starts, from the save menu, a script or a link feature.

events.name: save.done

payload.name: ok
payload.meaning: save.done only: the save was written

events.when: A save step returns. The payload says whether the write was accepted.

events.name: save.load
caveats: save.load's state_in_step reads 0. Whether the mod's own saved data was written with this save is a per-mod answer, and the payload is built once for every handler of the event, so the byte cannot carry it. The mod asks the services table instead (docs/mod-services.md, "The mod's own saved data").

payload.name: play_seconds
payload.meaning: play time of the loaded save

payload.name: state_in_step
payload.meaning: reads 0: whether the mod's own saved data was written with this save is a per-mod answer, and the payload is built once for every handler of the event, so the mod asks the services table's state_in_step (docs/mod-state.md, section 2)

events.when: A save is loaded, when the game data is read from it.

events.name: game.cleared
events.binding: EVENT_GAMECLEAR_Create 0x0215F8A8, the ending: Hall of Fame (ov180), credits (ov181), save screen (ov205)

payload.name: play_seconds
payload.meaning: play time at the Hall of Fame

events.when: The ending begins: Hall of Fame, credits, then the save screen.

events.name: route.change
events.when: The game sets up a new zone, on every map change.

events.name: map.warp
caveats: map.warp's arrival cell reads 0 for a warp to a rail position: the game names the rail cell of the destination in its own way. The event fires once per step of the map change, and the destination a handler changes is the one the game applies at the step that moves the player.
events.when: A warp is about to move the player. A handler may change the destination.

events.name: player.step
events.when: The game checks step events after the player moves one cell.

events.name: trainer.spotted
events.refuse: the trainer does not see the player (the function returns no event)

payload.name: trainer_id
payload.meaning: the trainer who saw the player

payload.name: partner_id
payload.meaning: the second trainer of a double, or 0

events.when: A trainer looks for the player in line of sight. Refusing makes the trainer miss the player.

events.name: npc.talk
events.refuse: no person is found ahead; the A press goes on to the sign and tile checks
caveats: npc.talk's object and script read 0. The model in front of the player is what the bound search returns, and the port does not run the search a second time to name it; the script the talk runs is the event id of that model, which the game reads when the search has answered.

payload.name: object_id
payload.meaning: the person or object talked to

events.when: The player presses A and the game looks for a person in front. Refusing finds nobody.

events.name: menu.open
events.binding: EVENT_FIELD_MENU_Create 0x0215FC40 (the X-button menu event) and EVENT_FIELD_MENU_CreateForZone 0x0215FCE0
events.refuse: the menu does not open (no event is returned)
caveats: game.new and menu.open have no fields at all: the event is the moment itself.
events.when: The X-button menu is about to open. Refusing keeps it shut.

events.name: menu.build
events.modifyText: entries (a cleared entry is hidden; one added is not built)
caveats: menu.build can hide an entry but cannot add one. The game prints the label of a slot and draws its icon from the message bank and the archive it opens while it creates the menu, and it closes both again, so the port cannot make a slot the game left empty. The slot keeps the label the game printed for it.

payload.name: entries
payload.meaning: one bit per menu entry shown

events.when: The X-button menu has just been built. A handler may hide entries.

events.name: field.move
events.refuse: the field move shows as unusable
caveats: field.move's user reads 0. The Pokemon that uses the move is the one the game's own handler for that move looks for in the party, and the port names neither the move the index stands for nor the member that has it.
events.when: The game asks whether a field move can be used. Refusing removes it from the choices.

events.name: pc.open
events.binding: SCRCMD_PROC_FLD_CallOv170Event 0x021B4D60, the script command that opens the box screen (the PC, and the battle box with its kind 4)
events.refuse: the PC does not open; the script reads a plain exit
events.when: A script opens the box screen (the PC, or the battle box).

events.name: encounter.wild
events.binding: the return of FIELD_ENCOUNT_CreateZoneWildMons 0x021A954C; roamers the return of FIELD_ENCOUNT_PickRoamer 0x021A957C
events.refuse: no battle; the player keeps walking; the payload names the area, the method (grass, surf, fishing, shaking grass) and the slot
events.modifyText: species, level, shiny; the second Pokemon of a double; a reroll
caveats: encounter.wild's species, level and shiny are the ones the game builds the wild Pokemon from. For a roamer the slot reads 0, because a roamer comes from the save and not from a table of the zone, and the roamer's shiny and double flags read 0 as well: its personality is the save's own and the game sets its battle up alone.

payload.name: method
payload.meaning: grass, dark grass, surf, fishing, shaking grass, rippling water, dust

payload.name: reroll
payload.meaning: version 4: 1 rolls the encounter again with the game's own roll and fires the event again, at most 16 times; the last answer stands

payload.name: level2
payload.meaning: version 4: the second Pokemon of a double (dark grass), 0 when there is none

events.when: A wild Pokemon was rolled for the area the player walks in. A handler may change it or cancel the battle.

events.name: encounter.static
caveats: encounter.static's legendary kind has no feeder at this call: the game chooses the species in the script that starts the battle, and the setup carries no flag for it. The kind the payload does carry says whether the battle is a wild one or a battle a script started. A species a handler changes is written into the record without the personal data being recalculated, so a mod that wants that uses the state calls.
events.when: A script starts a battle with a fixed Pokemon, such as a legendary or a gift battle.

events.name: encounter.trainer
events.when: A trainer battle is being set up.

events.name: mon.create
caveats: mon.create's nature reads 0xFF, the sentinel "leave the roll", because the nature is rolled inside the creation call. The shiny flag reads 0 on the creation row, because the roll is the caller's there; on the row that rolls the personality it is the caller's own request, and a handler that asks for a shiny Pokemon gets one through the applier. The personality is the argument the caller passes, the low half of the 64-bit value, which is the half the game stores; on the row that rolls the personality it reads 0 instead, because the game rolls it inside that call.

payload.name: nature
payload.meaning: the nature, or 0xFF to leave the roll

payload.name: personality
payload.meaning: the personality value the game rolled

events.when: The game creates a Pokemon record, for any reason. A handler may change species, level, shininess and nature.

events.name: mon.receive
events.binding: catch EVENT_BATTLE_RETURN_Main 0x021B9614 (ov092, the store step); gifts SCRCMD_PROC_AddMonToParty 0x0215C510, SCRCMD_PROC_AddMonToBox 0x0215C4C8, SCRCMD_PROC_AddEggToParty 0x0215C2D0 (ov010); SCRCMD_POKEMON_FLD_ReceiveGiftMon 0x021B6F18, daycare egg SODATEYA_ReceiveEgg 0x021C32F4 (ov021); in-game trade FLD_TRADE_CreateEvent 0x021CC500 (ov021)
notes: fires after the Pokemon is stored, from the functions that give the player a Pokemon. POKEPARTY_Add is not a binding: it also builds trainer parties, wild battle parties and battle copies. The event is not refusable because each receive path prints its own "sent to the PC" or "received" text before or after storing; a mod that limits the party moves the Pokemon with a state call and says so with a message.
caveats: mon.receive's slot reads 0 for a Pokemon that went into a box: the free slot inside that box is not named by the call. A Pokemon given while the party was full has no record left to read at all, so its shiny flag reads 0 as well and the species and level come from the script's own creation request. For an in-game trade the species reads 0: the trade record is the overlay's own data and the call does not name it, so a mod reads the Pokemon it is given through the state calls.

payload.name: source
payload.meaning: catch, gift, static, egg, in-game trade

payload.name: to_box
payload.meaning: it goes to a box because the party is full

events.when: The player gets a Pokemon: caught, gifted, an egg or an in-game trade. It fires after the Pokemon is stored.

events.name: mon.nickname
events.modifyText: force the prompt (marked, but the row carries no applier, so a write to it has no effect)
caveats: mon.nickname's Pokemon reads 0 on the prompt's own row: the prompt's work holds it, and that work is the overlay's own block, and the game's own code shows that the prompt never names a Pokemon at all (its three modes edit the player's greeting, the player's thanks message and the beacon message). The row that does name a Pokemon is the catch registration screen's own, and it carries the caught Pokemon; the party position reads 0 there, because the Pokemon is not in the party yet (the battle return stores it after the prompt). The force flag reads 0 as well: the game decides to ask before it gets to the prompt, and the catch screen's decision is not a declared row, so the port has no hook there.

payload.name: mon
payload.meaning: the Pokemon; empty on the prompt's own row, the caught Pokemon on the catch screen's

payload.name: force
payload.meaning: 1 opens the prompt even when the game would skip it (reads 0; the row has no applier)

events.when: The name prompt opens, or the catch screen offers a nickname.

events.name: mon.evolve
events.refuse: no evolution starts; an evolution stone has no effect
notes: the function is a check; its result 0 means no evolution in all ten callers (level-up, stones, trades).
events.when: The game checks whether a Pokemon evolves, after a level-up, with a stone or on a trade. Refusing stops the evolution.

events.name: mon.exp
events.binding: the return of BTL_SERVER_FLOW_CalcPartyExpShares 0x021CB2D4 (ov093); daycare SODATEYA_GrantExp 0x021C3530 (ov021)
notes: changes the amounts before the battle server records them, so the server, the battle display and the saved Pokemon agree. A level cap lowers the amount; refusing mon.levelup itself would leave the display showing a level the Pokemon does not have.
caveats: mon.exp names one Pokemon: the first member of the party that gains experience, because the payload has room for one. The experience and the level it carries are the party record's own, read through the state calls, because the battle works on a copy and those are the values the battle started from. The day care's payload has no party position: the call carries the Pokemon, not the party.

payload.name: wild
payload.meaning: version 4: for a battle, 1 when the battle is a wild one

events.when: Experience from a battle or the Day Care is about to be added. A handler may change the amount.

events.name: mon.levelup
events.binding: the return of BTL_POKEPARAM_AddExp 0x021D69B8, inside BTL_SERVER_FLOW_ApplyPartyExp 0x021C5350 (the level crossing)
events.when: A Pokemon in battle gains a level. It fires once for the level crossing.

events.name: move.learn
events.binding: level-up POKE_TOOL_GetLevelUpMove 0x02018328 (arm9); daycare SODATEYA_LearnMove 0x021C360C (ov021); the party screen's POKELIST_TryLearnMove 0x021BA5B4 and POKELIST_ReplaceMoveSlot 0x021BA5E0 (ov091); the nurse's relearner POKE_SUMMARY_MAIN_ApplyMove 0x021B6B0C (ov173); the script command that writes a move SCRCMD_PROC_SetMonMove 0x0215BD2C (ov010)
events.refuse: the level-up, the day care and the script: the move is not learned. The party screen's rows and the relearner's cannot be refused; the payload names the move and the source
notes: at POKE_TOOL_GetLevelUpMove: the function scans the learnset and writes the move into the Pokemon. A refused move is skipped: the refusal advances the scan past the entry and returns the "already known" code (0xFFFE), which every caller treats as nothing learned. The day care's row is refused the same way, by writing nothing, and the script command that writes a move is refused by answering 0, which is the answer it gives in every path of its own. The party screen's rows and the nurse's relearner screen print what they are about to do before they write it, so a refusal there would leave the game telling the player something false: they carry no refusal function, and a mod that wants to stop a learn reacts after the fact through the state calls.
caveats: move.learn's move slot is the first of the Pokemon's four that is empty, or 0xFF when it holds four moves already, on the three rows that name no slot: the level-up check, the day care and the party screen's first row. The other three name the slot they write into, and their replaced move is the move that was in that slot before the write. The three that name no slot read 0 for the replaced move, because the game asks for that later, in the screen that owns the choice.

move.learn fires from all six rows the area binds: the level-up check (arm9), the day care (ov021), the party screen's two (POKELIST_TryLearnMove 0x021BA5B4 and POKELIST_ReplaceMoveSlot 0x021BA5E0, ov091) and the nurse's relearner screen (POKE_SUMMARY_MAIN_ApplyMove 0x021B6B0C, ov173) are declared rows with the event in their fourth column, and the script command that writes a move (SCRCMD_PROC_SetMonMove 0x0215BD2C, ov010) is one too.  The party screen's rows and the relearner's read the game's own blocks (the screen's argument block, copied member for member from the game's header), so they name the move, the teacher and the slot; the script command's row reads the command's own operands, and its source reads 0 - the command names no teacher, and the tutor's own move table lives in ov021's script command, which the ARM9 builder cannot reach.

payload.name: source
payload.meaning: level, TM, tutor, relearner; 0 also stands for the rows that name no teacher

payload.name: slot
payload.meaning: the move slot it goes into, or 0xFF when the row names none

events.when: A Pokemon is about to learn a move by level-up, the Day Care, a TM or tutor, the move relearner or a script.

events.name: mon.release
events.binding: BOX2_MAIN_ClearSlot 0x021DD314, whose only caller is the release step BOX2_SEQ_StateMoveItemF 0x021E81D0, not inside BOX2_MAIN_UpdateBoxSlots
events.refuse: the Pokemon stays; the box redraws it
events.when: The player releases a Pokemon from the PC box screen.

events.name: box.deposit
events.binding: BOX2_MAIN_UpdateBoxSlots 0x021DD530, a party Pokemon placed in a box
events.refuse: the move is not applied; the box screen's own next step redraws the icons

payload.name: mon
payload.meaning: the Pokemon, where it is now

payload.name: box
payload.meaning: the box it moves into or out of

events.when: The player puts a party Pokemon into a box on the PC screen.

events.name: box.withdraw
events.binding: BOX2_MAIN_UpdateBoxSlots 0x021DD530, a box Pokemon placed in the party
events.refuse: as box.deposit

payload.name: mon
payload.meaning: the Pokemon, where it is now

payload.name: box
payload.meaning: the box it moves into or out of

events.when: The player takes a Pokemon out of a box into the party on the PC screen.

events.name: party.swap
events.refuse: the order does not change; the party screen redraws from the party
events.when: Two party members change places.

events.name: mon.helditem
notes: is not refusable: each of the five callers prints its "was given" text after the call. A mod that forbids held items takes the item back with a state call.
caveats: mon.helditem's party position is the one the party screen's own block names: the screen's argument block holds the party it shows, and the Pokemon the call carries is a member of it, so the port reads the position out of that party the way the screen does.
events.when: The party screen gives a Pokemon a held item.

events.name: egg.hatch
events.when: A script starts an egg hatch.

events.name: trade.ingame
events.refuse: the trade does not happen and the script goes on
caveats: trade.ingame's received species reads 0: the trade record is the overlay's own data and the call does not name it. The trade id and the party position are the command's own operands, and the port reads them out of the script's variables without moving the script VM's program counter.
events.when: A script starts an in-game trade. Refusing cancels it and the script goes on.

events.name: battle.start
events.binding: BTL_SETUP_Create 0x02013090 (arm9); the return of the setups: the wild BTL_SETUP_SetupWild 0x0201347C (arm9), the trainer FIELD_ENCOUNT_SetupTrainerBattle 0x021AA5CC (ov021), the scripted EVENT_BATTLE_CreateScriptedBattle 0x0216E7C8 (ov010)
events.modifyText: format, levels; the payload names the trainer ids and whether the battle is wild
caveats: battle.start's wild flag, format, trainer ids and the handle of the opposing party read 0 at the row that creates the setup: the setup the game will build does not exist yet.  The rows that build it (the wild setup, the trainer setup and the scripted one) fill them, and the port applies the format and the levels the handlers asked for.

payload.name: wild
payload.meaning: a wild battle; 0 at the row that creates the setup

payload.name: format
payload.meaning: single, double, triple, rotation, multi; 0xFF where the port does not know the format yet (the row that creates the setup)

payload.name: level_adjust
payload.meaning: added to every opposing Pokemon's level

payload.name: opponent_party
payload.meaning: a handle to the opposing party; a handler edits it through the state calls

events.when: A battle is created, then again when its setup is built. A handler may change the format and the opponent levels.

events.name: battle.action
events.binding: fight BTL_CLIENT_IsMoveSelectionBlocked 0x021CF5B0; run BTL_CLIENT_GetEscapeBlockerForSide 0x021CF918 (inside BTL_CLIENT_StepSelectRun); switch the return of BTL_PICK_GetLast 0x0689CB1C (ov095, inside BTL_CLIENT_StepSelectSwitchTarget)
events.refuse: the choice is not accepted and the action menu stays; the payload names the action and, for fight, the move
caveats: battle.action's Pokemon reads 0 for the switch: the choice list holds the party positions and nothing else. The party position the player picked is the function's result, and 6 is the game's own "backed out".

payload.name: side
payload.meaning: 0 the player's, 1 the opponent's (the AI asks the move check too)

events.when: The game checks a fight, switch or run choice. For a fight it fires several times a turn, once per move checked.

events.name: battle.item
events.binding: the return of BTLV_CORE_GetSelectedItem 0x021EA01C, inside BTL_CLIENT_StepSelectItem
events.refuse: back to the action menu; the item stays in the bag and the turn is not spent

payload.name: item
payload.meaning: the item chosen from the bag

payload.name: mon
payload.meaning: the Pokemon whose turn it is

payload.name: revive
payload.meaning: the item revives a fainted Pokemon

events.when: The player picks an item from the bag in battle. Refusing returns to the action menu.

events.name: battle.switch
notes: fires for every send-out, including after a faint and forced switches; it cannot be refused there, because the server has already committed the slot. A switch the player chooses is refused at battle.action.

payload.name: out
payload.meaning: the Pokemon leaving, or empty after a faint

payload.name: forced
payload.meaning: the switch follows a faint or a move that forces it

events.when: A Pokemon is sent out in battle, including after a faint.

events.name: battle.escape
events.refuse: the escape fails as a failed run: "Can't escape!" and the turn is spent
events.when: A run attempt is resolved. Refusing makes it fail and spends the turn.

events.name: battle.move
caveats: battle.move's target reads 0. The call carries the attacker and the move record, and the move record holds no target: the server picks the target set itself.
events.when: A Pokemon uses a move.

events.name: battle.damage
events.modifyText: the amount; the payload names attacker, target, move and the target's HP before
caveats: battle.damage fires on the return of the game's own function, so the amount is known: the port writes it into the word the caller reads. The target's HP before the hit is filled, because the hit has not landed yet (in a multi-hit move the earlier hits have).

payload.name: target_hp
payload.meaning: the target's HP before the hit

payload.name: effectiveness
payload.meaning: no effect, not very, neutral, super effective

events.when: The game has computed a hit and not applied it. A handler may change the amount.

events.name: battle.faint
notes: mon is a battle reference (place BW_MON_BATTLE); side 0 is the player's. cause, cause_move and cause_damage are empty or 0 when the faint came from weather, a hazard or a status.
A whiteout has its own event, whiteout. It is not the same moment as a single faint.
caveats: battle.faint's cause comes from the battle context, and a faint from the weather, a hazard or a status has no cause, so those fields read 0.

payload.name: cause_damage
payload.meaning: the last damage, or 0 for weather, a hazard or a status

events.when: A Pokemon faints in battle, from either side. Poison on the field never faints a Pokemon in this game (it stops at 1 HP).

events.name: catch.attempt
events.refuse: the ball is blocked as in a trainer battle: the block message shows, the ball stays in the bag, the turn is spent; the payload names the ball and the target's species and level
notes: uses the trainer-battle path of the same function: BTL_SERVER_FLOW_TryThrowBall returns 0 and pushes the block command (0x47), and its caller only takes the ball from the bag on 1. A mod that wants the ball and the turn kept refuses battle.item for balls instead.
caveats: catch.attempt's rate is the game's own rate as a percentage of its factor (the factor is a 12.12 fixed-point number and one is 0x1000), and the port answers the roll with the game's own factor scaled by the percentage a handler wrote. A mod that wants the absolute factor overrides the function that computes it, which is a declared row.

payload.name: rate
payload.meaning: the catch rate the roll uses, as a percentage of the game's own factor

events.when: The player throws a ball. A handler may change the catch rate or block the ball.

events.name: catch.result
caveats: catch.result fires at the return of the game's own roll (BTL_SERVER_FLOW_CalcCaptureShakes), not at the throw: the roll is where the game knows whether the Pokemon was caught and how many shakes it took. The caught flag is the roll's own result and the shakes are the ones the roll wrote into the word it was given; the target and the ball are the roll's own arguments, so the port does not run the throw's search again to name them.
events.when: The catch roll has finished. The payload says whether it caught and how many times the ball shook.

events.name: battle.end
events.when: The battle is over and the game reports the result.

events.name: whiteout
caveats: whiteout's money lost reads 0. The game computes the penalty inside the step, at the state that shows the amount, and the accessor that computes it latches its result, so the port does not call it: the game would find nothing left to show. The field half of the event reads 0 for the same reason: the recover script takes the money, and the port does not read the script's work.

payload.name: in_battle
payload.meaning: 1 the battle half, 0 the field half

events.when: The player's whole team has fainted. It fires for the battle part and for the field part.

events.name: battle.trainer_mon
events.binding: the rows that build a trainer battle's setup (battle.start), once per opposing member
events.modifyText: species, level, item, moves, ability, form
events.when: Once for each Pokemon of the opposing trainer, in party order, after the game builds the party and before the battle starts. A rule may change the level, species, item, moves, ability and form.

events.name: item.add
notes: is not refusable: its sixteen callers include the shop, which has taken the money before it adds the item. A count of 0 leaves the item out while the game's text says it was received.
events.when: An item is added to the bag, from any source. A handler may change the count.

events.name: item.use
events.refuse: the game's "it won't have any effect"; the item stays
notes: binds to the check the party screen runs before it applies an item; the "no effect" message is the game's own path for an unusable item.
caveats: item.use's target's party position reads 0: the call carries the party record but not the party, and the party is the party screen's own work. The record's address is in the handle, so a mod that has the party can find the position itself.

payload.name: target
payload.meaning: the Pokemon it is used on, or empty

events.when: The party screen checks whether an item can be used on a Pokemon. Refusing gives the game's 'no effect' text.

events.name: shop.buy
events.refuse: back to the item list; no money changes hands
notes: binds to the step that checks the money and the bag space after the player picks an item. The price is read there, so a changed price is the one the shop shows and charges. SCRCMD_PROC_FLD_PayPrice is not a binding: it runs after the "here you are" text and before the item is added.

payload.name: price
payload.meaning: the price of one; the shop shows and charges it

events.when: The player picks an item and a quantity in a shop. A handler may change the price.

events.name: money.change
caveats: money.change cannot be applied in the other direction on the row it fired on. The row that adds the money applies only a positive change and the row that takes it away applies only a negative one; a change of the other sign is applied as 0 and the money stays as it was. A mod that wants the money to go down waits for the row that takes it away.
events.when: Money is added or taken. A handler may change the amount, but only in the direction of the call.

events.name: heal
events.binding: SCRCMD_PROC_HealParty 0x0215B5A8 (ov010, a centre or a script); GPOWER_UseHpRestore 0x0201104C (arm9, the HP-restore power)
events.refuse: the heal does not happen; the script's own text still plays
notes: POKE_TOOL_HealParty is not a binding; it also heals link, musical and infrared battle parties.
caveats: heal's source reads as script for a Pokemon Centre, because the nurse runs the same script command and the two cannot be told apart at the call. The mask names the party positions the heal covers, and the port heals the positions a handler kept with the game's own healer; it cannot take the heal away from a position the game's own function heals, because that function heals every occupied slot and there is no hook between its heal and its return. A mod that wants a narrower heal refuses the event and then heals the Pokemon it wants through the state calls.

payload.name: source
payload.meaning: Pokemon Centre or script, the HP-restore power

payload.name: mask
payload.meaning: one bit per party position to heal

events.when: A heal starts, at a Pokemon Centre, from a script or from the HP-restore power. A handler may choose who heals.

events.name: heal.hp
events.binding: PLIST_DEMO_RestoreHp 0x021BE914 (ov091, an item on the field); BTL_SERVER_FLOW_ApplyHpRecover 0x021C33E8 (ov093, every restore in a battle)
events.refuse: no HP is added
notes: source is 0 (BW_HEAL_HP_FIELD) on the field and 1 (BW_HEAL_HP_BATTLE) in a battle. The amount is capped at max HP after the handler runs.
On the field the item is used up even when the restore is refused: refuse item.use to keep it.

payload.name: mon
payload.meaning: the Pokemon that gets HP back

payload.name: amount
payload.meaning: the HP to add, before the cap at max HP

payload.name: source
payload.meaning: field (an item from the bag or the party screen) or battle (any restore: bag item, held item, move, ability)

events.when: The game is about to add HP to a Pokemon. On the field it fires when the party screen restores HP with an item. In a battle it fires for every HP restore, through BTL_SERVER_FLOW_ApplyHpRecover: a bag item, a berry, Leftovers, a move or an ability. A handler may change the amount, or refuse to add nothing.

events.name: badge.get
events.when: A badge is set. It fires after the badge is held.

events.name: flag.set
events.when: The game sets an event flag.

events.name: dex.register
events.when: A species is registered as seen or caught.

state.name: money
state.value: the player's money

state.name: badges
state.value: the number of badges

actions.name: refuse
actions.what: Refuses the event. Valid only on events that can be refused; the game then takes the event's refused outcome.

actions.name: set
actions.what: Assigns a payload field marked writable, a writable state field, or a mod cell.

actions.name: message
actions.what: Shows a line of text to the player.

actions.name: send
actions.what: Sends a value to the peers of the current session.

actions.name: release
actions.what: Releases a Pokemon of the player's party for good. It is applied at the first player step on the field after a battle, and not when it would leave only eggs.

actions.name: box
actions.what: Moves a party Pokemon to box n, counted from 0. It is applied at the next field step. It fails when the box is full, and not when it would leave only eggs.

actions.name: withdraw
actions.what: Moves the Pokemon at a box and slot to the party. It is applied at the next field step. It fails when the party is full or the slot is empty.

actions.name: give
actions.what: Puts a number of an item in the bag at once. Nothing happens when the bag cannot take it, and the rule stops for that firing.

functions.name: mon_to_box
functions.what: Moves a party Pokemon to the first free box slot. The port queues it and applies it when no battle, party screen or PC holds the party open.

functions.name: mon_take_item
functions.what: Returns a Pokemon's held item to the bag. Queued like mon_to_box.

functions.name: mon_release
functions.what: Releases a Pokemon of the player's party for good. It takes a party reference or a reference to one of the player's Pokemon in battle. The release is queued and applied at the first player step on the field after the battle; the Pokemon is found by its personality value then, so a switch or a compaction cannot hit the wrong one. It is refused when it would leave the party with no Pokemon that is not an egg. The party compacts and the next member becomes the lead.

functions.what: How many of an item the bag holds.

functions.what: Puts a number of an item in the bag at once.
functions.result: 0 on success. Non-zero when the item is past the item limit, the count is 0 or the pocket is full; a refused add puts nothing in.

functions.result: 1 for a wild battle, 0 for a trainer's, -1 when no battle runs.

functions.what: The play time of the save in force, in seconds.

functions.what: Reads one data field of an item, by the game's field id.
functions.result: 0 on success; non-zero past the item limit.

functions.name: move_value

functions.result: 0 on success; non-zero past the move limit.

functions.what: Moves a party Pokemon to a named box (0 is the first). Queued like mon_to_box and applied at the next field step. It fails when the box is full, and it never leaves the party without a Pokemon that is not an egg.

functions.what: Moves the Pokemon at a box and slot to the party. Queued like mon_to_box. It fails when the party is full or the slot is empty.

functions.name: mon_recalc
functions.what: Works out a party Pokemon's level and stats again from its species, experience, IVs and EVs, as the game does after a level up. Call it after party_set changes any of those. It does not work on a box or battle reference.

functions.name: message
functions.what: Shows a line of text in the game's message window. It is queued and shown at the next point where the game accepts a message. Text is UTF-8; characters the font lacks show as ?.

functions.name: confirm
functions.what: Asks a yes/no question in the field. In battle it answers 0 at once.

functions.name: session_host
functions.what: Starts a peer session through the relay and returns its code. It blocks for up to three seconds.

functions.name: session_join

functions.name: session_leave
functions.what: Leaves the session.

functions.what: Sends up to 4 KB to one peer, or to everyone with peer 0. Only the same mod on the other side receives it.

functions.name: on_session
functions.what: Sets the handler for peer messages, joins and leaves. It runs on the game frame.

functions.name: setting_get
functions.what: Reads one of the mod's own options (declared in the file named by the manifest's settings key). The key is the one on the option's line.
functions.result: 0 or 1 for a bool, the index of the chosen name for a choice, the number for an int option, -1 for a key the mod does not declare.

blocks.text: A raw hook replaces or wraps one game function from the list below. It is for code mods only, with the game's own arguments. Prefer events and rules; use a hook when no event covers what you need.
In kenon, one hook is one line in the Hooks view: `region:address mode symbol`. The symbol is a function exported by your mod's code.
ov093:0x021CBD48 wrap my_catch_rate sig="int (void)" switch=my_catch

items: `wrap` runs your function in place of the game's and lets you call the original through the chain. Several wraps nest, the last loaded runs first.
`replace` takes the function for itself. When two mods replace one function, the later mod wins and the other is reported as shadowed.
`sig` states the prototype you expect, as `"<return> (<parameters>)"`. The port refuses the hook when it differs from the function's own.
A hook is keyed by region and address, never by name, because names change when the decompilation is cleaned up.
The game's arguments can change when the code is restructured. A mod with raw hooks states the port version it was built for.

blocks.text: Rows with events are already bound to a stable event: that event fires from the same function.

A code mod is C. It exports eidos_mod_start and eidos_mod_stop, binds handlers to events with `on`, and reaches the game only through the state calls and services listed here. It cannot call game functions directly; raw hooks replace or wrap them.

A handler gets the event payload and returns CONTINUE or REFUSE. It may write the payload fields marked writable; the port reads them back before the game goes on. A write to any other field has no effect. A refusal at an event that cannot be refused is ignored and logged once.

items: The snippets in these docs use the native header (mod_api.h and mod_state.h, api 4), which is what the port loads today. A mod built for api 3 still loads.
The WebAssembly build (api 4) keeps the same event, payload and service names. Its headers come with eidos's published api, and the build in the Code view uses the current draft header until then.
No libc and no WASI in the wasm build: a mod reaches nothing outside the game except through the port's imports.

blocks.text: Several handlers on one event all run, in load order. Writes chain and any refusal refuses. The battle works on a copy of each Pokemon: during a battle read and write the battle record (battle_get, battle_set), not the party record.
A rule acts on one event without any code. It has an event, zero or more guards (`when`) and one or more actions (`do`). It has no loops, functions, local variables or branches.
A rule file holds one rule. The manifest binds the file to its event with a `rule = <event> <path>` line; the event in the file must match.

language 1
rule faint_penalty on battle.faint
    when event.side == 0
    do sub money 1000

items: Several `when` lines must all hold.
A rule that reaches 256 steps stops for that firing without refusing.
Division or modulo by zero gives 0. An unset cell reads 0.
Several mods on one event all run, in load order. Writes chain and any refusal refuses.

blocks.text: Need a loop, a search of the party, a fallback or anything beyond this? Write a code mod; the two mix in one mod.

Read a payload field as `event.<field>`. Read the game through state fields such as `money` or `level[event.mon]`. Keep your own data in `state.<cell>`; with a subscript it is a keyed table, up to 1024 keys, saved with the game.

head: Type
Values
rows: A 32-bit signed number. Every numeric payload and state field.
true or false. Comparisons and flag fields.
A Pokemon reference. Use it as a subscript: hp[event.mon].

blocks.text: Operators, loosest to tightest: `||`, `&&`, `!`, comparisons (`== != < <= > >=`), `+ -`, `* / %`, unary `-`. Both sides of a comparison must have the same type; arithmetic needs int. There are no names for enum values: use the numbers listed on the event page.
Read the mod's own options as `setting.<key>` (see Options) and its data tables as `table.<name>[key]`.
Operators are read as two characters at most. A pair that is not an operator reads as two, so `x*-1` and `a<-1` mean what they look like.

head: Target
Writable when
rows: The payload page marks the field writable. Any other field is a load error.
The state field page says the port can write it.
Always. The cell belongs to your mod.

blocks.text: The game's later write wins. To make a change stick, write the payload field of the event the game derives the value from, not the state field after it.
A table is a file of numbers the mod reads by key: a level cap for each badge count, a list of banned species, a zone-to-area map. Rules and code read it. What the table means is up to the mod.
Declare each table with one line in the manifest. The Tables view writes it for you.
table = caps tables/caps.txt

items: The name is letters, digits and `_`, does not start with a digit, and has at most 31 characters.
The path is inside the mod folder.
A mod can hold up to 128 tables in all, counting every loaded mod.
A table belongs to the mod that declares it. Two mods can each have a table called `caps`; neither reads the other's.

blocks.text: The file has one entry per line. A key and a value are signed 32-bit numbers, written in decimal or with `0x` for hex. `#` starts a comment. `default = N` is the value of every key the table does not list, and 0 when there is no such line.

# level cap per badge count
0 = 12
1 = 20     # after the first gym
0x2 = 25
default = 100

items: When a key is listed twice, the later line wins. The checker warns about it.
A table holds up to 65536 entries, and the file is at most 16 MiB.
A table that fails to load is reported when the game starts. The mod's other tables and rules still load.

blocks.text: A rule reads a table with `table.<name>[key]`. The key is any number expression, such as `badges`. A key the table lacks reads the default.

language 1
rule level_cap on mon.exp
    when level[event.mon] >= table.caps[badges]
    do set event.amount 0
A rule that names a table the mod does not declare is refused when the game loads it. The checker reports the same error. Code reads a table with `table_get(name, key, &out)`.

A mod can show options on the game's settings screen, under its own name. The player picks a value, the game keeps it beside the mod's saved data, and the mod reads it. Declare the options in a file and name it in the manifest. The Options tab of Mod settings writes both.
settings = options.txt
The file has one option per line: `option <key> <kind> "<label>" <value>`. `#` starts a comment, anywhere on a line. A line that does not start with `option` is skipped.

option dupes   bool    "Dupes clause"    on
option cap     choice  "Level caps"      off|gym|ace
option lives   int     "Lives"           0 10 3

head: Kind
Value
Reads as
rows: `on` or `off`. Any text other than `on`, `true` and `1` is off.
Up to 8 names split by `|`, 31 characters each. The first is the default.
The index of the chosen name
`<min> <max> <default>`, whole numbers within a billion of zero, with min <= default <= max. The screen steps by one.

items: The key is one word. It cannot hold `=` or `#`, and it has at most 63 characters.
The label is quoted, has no quote or `#`, and has at most 63 characters.
A mod has up to 16 options. The game ignores the rest.
A line the game cannot read is skipped. The checker reports it.
When a key is declared twice, the first answers.

blocks.text: A rule reads an option with `setting.<key>`. A rule key is letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit, so a key with a dot is for code only. A key the mod does not declare reads -1, and the checker warns about it. A mod with no namespace has no settings, and the game refuses a rule that reads one. Code reads an option with `setting_get(key)`.

language 1
rule lives on catch.attempt
    when setting.lives == 0
    do refuse

recipes.title: Lose money when a Pokemon faints
recipes.goal: Take 1000 money each time one of your Pokemon faints.
steps: `battle.faint` fires when a Pokemon faints. `event.side` is 0 for the player's side.
The rule guards on the side and subtracts from `money`.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule faint_penalty on battle.faint
    when event.side == 0
    do sub money 1000

recipes.title: Cap the level
recipes.goal: Stop a Pokemon from gaining experience once it reaches level 30.
steps: `mon.exp` fires before experience is added. `event.level` is the level before; `event.amount` is writable.
Setting the amount to 0 in the rule keeps the battle, the display and the saved Pokemon in agreement.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule level_cap on mon.exp
    when event.level >= 30
    do set event.amount 0
notes: Refusing `mon.levelup` instead would leave the screen showing a level the Pokemon does not have; lower the experience.

recipes.title: Block grass encounters before the first badge
recipes.goal: No wild battle in grass while the player has no badge.
steps: `encounter.wild` can be refused. `event.method` is 0 for grass.
`badges` is a state field with the number of badges.
A refused encounter is no battle; the player keeps walking.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule no_early_grass on encounter.wild
    when badges == 0 && event.method == 0
    do refuse

recipes.title: Make low-level Pokemon easier to catch
recipes.goal: Double the catch rate for wild Pokemon below level 20.
steps: `catch.attempt` fires when a ball is thrown. `event.level` is the target's level.
`event.rate` is the catch rate as a percentage of the game's own: 100 leaves it alone, 200 doubles it. It is a byte, so 255 is the most.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule easy_catch on catch.attempt
    when event.level < 20
    do set event.rate 200

recipes.title: Show a message on a level-up
recipes.goal: Tell the player when a Pokemon reaches a level that is a multiple of 10.
steps: `mon.levelup` fires once for the level crossing. `event.to` is the level reached.
`message` shows text in the game's window. The text is a fixed string.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule round_level on mon.levelup
    when event.to % 10 == 0
    do message "A round number!"

recipes.title: Pay a bonus for beating a trainer
recipes.goal: Add 500 money when the player wins a trainer battle.
steps: `battle.end` carries `outcome` (0 is a win) and `wild` (0 for a trainer battle).
The rule adds to `money`.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule trainer_bonus on battle.end
    when event.outcome == 0 && event.wild == 0
    do add money 500
notes: `money.change` does not say where money came from, so a rule that doubles prize money there would also double other income. Test before relying on it.

recipes.title: Every fished Pokemon is shiny
recipes.goal: Make fishing encounters shiny.
steps: `encounter.wild` lets a rule write `event.shiny`: 1 forces shiny, 0 leaves the roll.
`event.method` is 3 for fishing.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule shiny_fishing on encounter.wild
    when event.method == 3
    do set event.shiny 1

recipes.title: Forbid releasing Pokemon from the PC
recipes.goal: The release step does nothing and tells the player why.
steps: `mon.release` fires on the release step of the box screen and can be refused. The Pokemon stays; the box redraws it.
A refusal shows nothing by itself: add a `message`.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule keep_everyone on mon.release
    do refuse
    do message "These Pokemon stay."

recipes.title: One catch per route
recipes.goal: Allow one catch on each zone, then refuse more balls there.
steps: Two rules share a keyed cell: `state.route_used[zone]`. Cells are saved with the game.
`catch.result` sets the cell when `event.caught` is 1.
`catch.attempt` can be refused: the ball stays in the bag and the turn is spent.
A rule file holds one rule, so these are two files.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule mark_route_used on catch.result
    when event.caught == 1
    do set state.route_used[zone] 1
recipes.rule2:
language 1
rule one_catch_per_route on catch.attempt
    when state.route_used[zone] == 1
    do refuse
    do message "You already caught a Pokemon on this route."
notes: The first block is the rule for `catch.result`; the second is the rule for `catch.attempt`.

recipes.title: A setting that switches a feature
recipes.goal: Halve all experience when the player turns on an option in the port's settings screen.
steps: Declare the option in an options file and name it in the manifest with `settings = options.txt`. The Options tab of Mod settings writes both.
A rule reads the option as `setting.<key>`. It is 0 or 1 for a bool, the index for a choice.
In C, the handler for `mon.exp` reads the option with `setting_get`.
`amount` is writable, so both halve it before the game uses it.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule slow_exp on mon.exp
    when setting.slow_exp == 1
    do set event.amount event.amount / 2

recipes.title: Release a Pokemon when it faints
recipes.goal: A fainted Pokemon of the player is released for good (a Nuzlocke rule).
steps: `battle.faint` fires when a Pokemon faints. `event.side` is 0 for the player's side and `event.mon` is the fainted Pokemon.
`release` (in C, `mon_release`) queues the release. It is applied at the first player step on the field after the battle, so the battle is not disturbed.
It does nothing if the Pokemon is the last one that is not an egg.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule nuzlocke on battle.faint
    when event.side == 0
    do release event.mon
notes: Whiteout is a separate event, `whiteout`. Poison on the field does not faint a Pokemon in this game.

recipes.title: Give an item on entering a map
recipes.goal: Give 5 Potions the first time the player enters a zone.
steps: `route.change` fires on every map change; `event.zone` is the zone entered. Replace 115 with the zone you want.
`give <item> <count>` puts the items in the bag at once. If the bag cannot take them, the rule stops for that firing and tries again on the next entry.
The cell `state.gift_given` is saved with the game and reads 0 until it is set, so the gift is given once. The `give` line comes first, so the cell is set only after a successful gift.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule potion_gift on route.change
    when event.zone == 115 && state.gift_given == 0
    do give 17 5
    do set state.gift_given 1
notes: The C version keeps its flag in memory only. Save it with `state_store` to keep it across runs. `item_count[17]` reads the Potions the bag holds, for a rule that gives only when the bag has none.

recipes.title: Halve all healing
recipes.goal: Every HP restore gives half the HP, on the field and in battle.
steps: `heal.hp` fires before HP is added. `event.amount` is the HP to add and is writable.
The amount is capped at max HP after the rule runs.
`event.source` is 0 on the field and 1 in battle, so a `when` line can limit the rule to one of them.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule half_healing on heal.hp
    do set event.amount event.amount / 2

recipes.title: No HP restores in battle
recipes.goal: No Pokemon gets HP back during a battle, from any source.
steps: `heal.hp` can be refused; a refusal adds no HP. In battle it fires for every restore: bag items, berries, Leftovers, moves and abilities.
`event.source` is 1 for a battle.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule no_battle_healing on heal.hp
    when event.source == 1
    do refuse
notes: A bag item is still used up when its restore is refused. To stop the item from being used, refuse `battle.item`: the player returns to the action menu.

recipes.title: Count faints in the status panel
recipes.goal: Show how many of your Pokemon fainted this session beside the screens.
steps: `battle.faint` fires for both sides; `side` 0 is the player's.
`panel_set` writes one of the 16 panel lines.

recipes.title: Level cap by badge
recipes.goal: A Pokemon gains no experience once it reaches the level cap for the badges the player holds.
steps: Make a table called `caps` in the Tables view. Each key is a badge count and each value the highest level allowed. `default` covers every count the table does not list.
`mon.exp` fires once for each party member that gains experience. Setting `event.amount` to 0 gives that member none.
`table.caps[badges]` reads the cap for the badges the player holds now.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule level_cap on mon.exp
    when level[event.mon] >= table.caps[badges]
    do set event.amount 0
notes: The cap compares the level before the gain, as `event.level` and `level[event.mon]` both read it.

recipes.title: Rare Candy stops at the cap
recipes.goal: A Rare Candy cannot be used on a Pokemon that has reached the level cap.
steps: `item.use` fires when an item is used and can be refused. A refusal keeps the Rare Candy in the bag and the level as it was.
`event.item` is the item and `event.target` the Pokemon it is used on. Item 50 is the Rare Candy in the game's item list.
The cap comes from the `caps` table of the level cap recipe.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule candy_cap on item.use
    when event.item == 50 && level[event.target] >= table.caps[badges]
    do refuse
    do message "It cannot grow past the cap yet."

recipes.title: Roll again for a species the player owns
recipes.goal: A wild encounter of a species the player already owns is rolled again.
steps: `owned[s]` is 1 when the party or a box holds a Pokemon of species `s` that is not an egg.
`event.reroll` is writable. Setting it to 1 rolls the encounter again with the game's own roll and fires the event again, at most 16 times. The last roll stands.
A rule that refuses the event on a reroll leaves no encounter.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule dupes on encounter.wild
    when owned[event.species] == 1
    do set event.reroll 1
notes: To skip only the first stage of an evolution line, add `species_stage[event.species] == 0` to the guard.

recipes.title: Check types in the party
recipes.goal: Refuse a ball on a species without a type, and refuse wild encounters while the party has no Pokemon of that type.
steps: Type ids are the game's own: Water is 10.
`species_type1[s]` and `species_type2[s]` read a species' types. The first rule refuses the ball when neither is Water.
`party_has_type[t]` is 1 when a party Pokemon that is not an egg has type `t`. The second rule refuses the encounter when it is 0.
A rule file holds one rule, so these are two files.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule water_only on catch.attempt
    when species_type1[event.species] != 10 && species_type2[event.species] != 10
    do refuse
    do message "Only Water types."
recipes.rule2:
language 1
rule need_water on encounter.wild
    when party_has_type[10] == 0
    do refuse
notes: The first block is the rule for `catch.attempt`; the second is the rule for `encounter.wild`.

recipes.title: Use the play time
recipes.goal: Wild encounters start only after the save has an hour of play time.
steps: `play_seconds` is the play time of the save in seconds.
`encounter.wild` can be refused. The player keeps walking.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule slow_start on encounter.wild
    when play_seconds < 3600
    do refuse

recipes.title: Stronger second Pokemon in dark grass
recipes.goal: In a double battle from dark grass, the second wild Pokemon is two levels higher.
steps: `event.method` is 1 for dark grass and `event.double` is 1 for a double battle.
`event.level2` and `event.species2` are the second Pokemon of the double. Both are writable. `level2` is 0 when there is no second Pokemon.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule dark_grass_pair on encounter.wild
    when event.method == 1 && event.double == 1
    do add event.level2 2

recipes.title: Change a trainer's party
recipes.goal: Every Pokemon of every trainer is a number of levels higher, and the player picks the number.
steps: `battle.trainer_mon` fires once for each opposing Pokemon, in party order, after the game builds the party.
A new level works out the stats again. Writing 0 to `level`, `species` or `ability` keeps the game's value.
The option is a whole number. `setting.boost` reads it. It is declared in the options file with a lowest value, a highest value and a default.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule stronger_trainers on battle.trainer_mon
    do add event.level setting.boost

recipes.title: Change experience by source
recipes.goal: Wild battles give no experience.
steps: `event.source` is 0 for a battle and 1 for the day care.
`event.wild` is 1 when the battle is a wild one.
The event fires once for each member that gains experience, and an amount of 0 gives that member none.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule no_grinding on mon.exp
    when event.source == 0 && event.wild == 1
    do set event.amount 0

recipes.title: Move a Pokemon to a box
recipes.goal: A Pokemon of the player that faints is moved to box 23.
steps: `box <mon> <n>` moves a party Pokemon to box `n`, counted from 0. It is applied at the next field step, so the battle is not disturbed.
It fails when the box is full, and it never leaves the party without a Pokemon that is not an egg.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule graveyard on battle.faint
    when event.side == 0
    do box event.mon 23
